text.p: These are the headlines selected from Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Ontario cuts basic income-tax rate: Finance Minister highlights spending on health care, education, job creation.
- Bre-X plummets in record trading: Firm's shares fetch pennies.
- Chretien hazy on drug plan costs: 'Have to talk to the provinces".
- Emergency dikes may be permanent: Funding catch must be resolved first.
- 'Scapegoat' soldier plugs new book: Misjudged/ Disgraced trooper Brown says medication made him do it.
- Politics keeps lid on Korean famine relief: Worried about food going to North's army, Seoul and Washington want peace talks as price for help, while Japanese simply say no.
- Bre-X's winners and losers: The stock's collapse has left some investors richer, others wiser.
- Clues were plentiful that Busang a fraud: Red flags were in Kilborn report.
- First Marathon adds up losses: Half of dealer's 1st-quarter trading shortfall caused by Bre-X.
- Felderhof seen as key to Bre-X scandal: Bre-X geologist had direct control of shipping core samples, but he denies any involvement in Busang fraud.
- CP to place business hotels in $750M trust.
